area.reviews.1.quote: We had such a great experience with City and Suburban Heating and Cooling! Rob, the owner, is knowledgeable, professional, and honest. Our HVAC system was making a loud noise and we were worried it was going to be a major repair, but Rob quickly diagnosed the problem and had it fixed in no time. It turned out to be just the outer shell that was loose.
area.reviews.2.quote: Our AC unit is an oldie, but apparently a goodie, still kicking after 20 years. We're saving up for a new one but want to extend the life of this one as it died yesterday. City & Suburban was highly recommended by our neighbor. Rob scheduled the appointment literally the following morning after our call. His assessment fee was very reasonable... and you pay nothing if it can't be fixed.
area.reviews.3.quote: City & Suburban is the best. I struggled through a couple of other HVAC companies with poor results but City & Suburban is so much better to work with. Their techs are more knowledgeable, they solved a months long issue we were having in just a few minutes that several other companies' techs could not figure out after several appointments.
area.reviews.4.quote: City & Suburban Heating and Cooling has been an absolute lifesaver for me, and I cannot recommend them highly enough. Rob, the heart and soul behind this family-operated business, is not only a great guy but also a true professional who knows the ins and outs of heating and cooling systems. What sets them apart is not just their expertise but the genuine care and quick response they provide whenever…
area.scope.heading: The same repair costs differently in a three-flat, a cottage and a condo
area.scope.1.why: Many two- and three-flats here run one boiler for every unit, so a repair reaches every tenant and the owners decide together.
area.scope.2.why: Radiator-heated flats have no ducts for central air, so cooling usually means ductless mini-splits.
area.scope.3.why: On Haddon, Thomas and Cortez, work that changes the outside, like a condenser in view of the street, can need Landmarks review.
area.scope.4.why: Kerfoot's brick cottages sit on raised basements with low ceilings, which set how a furnace or boiler comes in and out.
area.scope.5.why: Storefronts and restaurants on Chicago Ave run rooftop units and kitchen exhaust, so roof access and opening hours set the work.
area.scope.6.why: The biggest swing of all. Where the unit has years left, we say so.

area.buildings.heading: What heats and cools your Ukrainian Village building
area.buildings.1.title: Brick two- or three-flat
area.buildings.1.body: A boiler for the whole building or a furnace per unit. Ductless cooling where radiators heat the flats.
area.buildings.2.title: Worker's cottage
area.buildings.2.body: A basement furnace or a small boiler under a raised first floor. Short duct runs, low basements.
area.buildings.3.title: New-build condo
area.buildings.3.body: A furnace or heat pump per unit, with central air. Condensers on the roof or a rear deck.
area.buildings.4.title: Storefront with flats
area.buildings.4.body: Rooftop units for the shop on Chicago Ave, a furnace or boiler for the flats above.

area.faq.heading: Ukrainian Village HVAC, answered
area.faq.1.q: Is the boiler in my three-flat worth repairing, or does it need replacing?
area.faq.1.a: Often it's worth repairing. We diagnose first, and where the boiler has years left, we say so. Replacement is quoted only when the repair stops making sense.
area.faq.2.q: How far is your shop from Ukrainian Village?
area.faq.3.q: Can you cool a radiator-heated three-flat without ductwork?
area.faq.4.q: Does HVAC repair in Chicago need a permit?
area.cta.body: Have the make of your boiler, furnace or condenser to hand, and tell us what it's doing. In a two- or three-flat, tell us which units share the boiler.

extras.faq.2.a: Under a mile. The shop is at 1225 N Cleaver St, east of the corner at Division and Damen, and Rob runs the calls from there.
extras.faq.3.a: Usually, yes. Radiator-heated flats have no ducts for central air, so cooling means ductless mini-splits, with the condenser off the alley or on a rear porch.
extras.faq.4.a: No. Chicago doesn't require a permit to repair, diagnose or maintain heating and cooling. Permits cover installs and construction, so a company's permit count says little about its repair work.

_sources.districts: Wikipedia (Ukrainian Village District): Chicago Landmark district (2002, extended 2005 and 2007) on Haddon, Thomas and Cortez between Damen and Leavitt; St. Nicholas Ukrainian Catholic Cathedral (Oakley and Rice), St. Volodymyr (Cortez and Oakley). East Village Association (2020): worker's cottages on Augusta between Leavitt and Damen.
_sources.buildings: Chicago Landmarks (Ukrainian Village District, Extension 3 report): brick two- and three-flats of 1892-1904 are the majority; about a third are brick worker's cottages built by William D. Kerfoot, 1886-1905. Area permit mix (furnace 4, ductwork 3, boiler 1, heat pump 1).
